Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! India Women donning the 'Pink Jersey' in this game to spread awareness about Breast Cancer, a great initiative from the hosts. However, they now need a big, big batting effort to chase this massive total. Out come the openers - Pratika Rawal and Smriti Mandhana. The Aussies are already out there, and it will be Megan Schutt to start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

A complete batting performance from Australia Women on the other hand. Their top five contributed massively with Beth Mooney taking the honours mostly. She hit her ton in just 57 balls while coming in when Australia Women were on track to score big. She made it light work but thanks to the openers for laying the foundation. Georgia Voll scored a quick-fire fifty at the top, while Alyssa Healy kept the intent as well. Ellyse Perry then picked up the baton to continue the merry way, but it was Beth Mooney who came in and scored boundaries for fun, including 23 boundaries and a six. Overall, Australia Women scored 60 boundaries, second most in an innings. India Women have left the field looking tired, but the job is not done yet. They have a mountain to climb. Can they chase it? Stay tuned to find out.

What must be going through that Indian team right now? Morale-boosting win in the second match to conceding more than 400 in a must-win match. Their bowlers have been taken to the cleaners. Australia Women have scored the highest first innings total against India. Once again, the fielding was under scrutiny as they lacked energy on the field and under the heat, they were made to chase the ball.

A drenched Indian team walk back after conceding more than 400 under scorching heat. Wow! This is how a champion team replies. After a heavy defeat, Australia Women needed to show a strong reply and how they have responded. Total dominance from Australia Women and they have one foot over the series now.

Commentary.Commentary: The stage is set for the series-decider between Australia Women and India Women! Alyssa Healy and Georgia Voll are walking out to open for Australia, while Kranti Gaud is ready to bowl the first over. With a lush green outfield and perfect batting conditions, expectations are high for a thrilling match filled with runs. Let's see how the game unfolds!

PITCH REPORT - Deep Dasgupta described the playing conditions at the Arun Jaitley Stadium, noting the hot and humid weather. He provided details about the ground's dimensions, with the straight boundary measuring 71m and the square boundaries around 62-63m. Rachel Haynes, joining Dasgupta, assessed the pitch as a fantastic batting surface, describing it as extremely flat with minimal grass. She also noted that the outfield feels lightning-fast, suggesting that there could be a high-scoring match. Haynes predicted that a score above 300 would be required, anticipating a lot of runs regardless of which team bats first.

India women's captain Harmanpreet Kaur emphasized the importance of playing good cricket with the right mindset. She stated that her team's focus is on performing their best cricket, which has kept them competitive in games. Kaur expressed her desire for the team to maintain a positive mindset in today's match. She also confirmed that the team will field the same XI, sticking to their approach and strategy.

Australia women's captain Alyssa Healy expressed her team's readiness to take on their opponents, emphasizing the importance of getting a good start to set the tone for the rest of the game. She acknowledged that their previous match against India didn't go well, but she's confident that her team can create pressure and perform better this time. Healy highlighted the challenge of adapting to different conditions, including playing under lights, which she sees as valuable preparation for the World Cup. She also announced two changes to the team - Kim Garth and Grace Harris will play, replacing Darcie Brown and Annabel Sutherland.
Australia Women (Playing XI) - Alyssa Healy (C)(WK), Georgia Voll, Ellyse Perry, Beth Mooney, Grace Harris, Ash Gardner, Tahlia McGrath, Georgia Wareham, Alana King, Kim Garth, Megan Schutt.

India Women (Playing XI) - Pratika Rawal, Smriti Mandhana, Harleen Deol, Harmanpreet Kaur (C), Deepti Sharma, Richa Ghosh (WK), Radha Yadav, Arundhati Reddy, Sneh Rana, Kranti Gaud, Renuka Singh Thakur.
TOSS - Australia Women have won the toss and they have decided to BAT first.

It wasn’t an easy road for India as they were beaten heavily in the first match. They looked tired and lacked confidence on the field, while also dropping too many catches while defending a par score. However, they bounced back solidly thanks to Mandhana’s sublime century at the top of the order. Their main ingredient in the victory was how the bowlers responded. Although they let away quite a few chances coming their way, the bowlers stuck to the plans and were the main architects of Australia’s downfall. There will be a lot of pressure on the visitors. Losing a series after a long period of time and that too right before the World Cup, could be morale-damaging. However, they are known as the mighty Aussies for a reason. They have been in similar positions before and have bounced back strongly. Let’s hope we get a thriller and may the best team win. Stay tuned for toss and other updates.

So many records were broken after India’s triumph against Australia to level the series 1-1. India ended an 18-year wait for a home ODI triumph against the Aussies. Not only this, it also snapped Australia’s 13-match winning streak in the format. India have a chance to create history by winning their first-ever WODI series win over Australia Women and what a boost it would give before the huge World Cup coming at home.

The stage is set for a high-stakes decider at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in Delhi, as India Women look to script history by clinching their first-ever WODI series win over Australia Women. The hosts come into the contest buoyed by a commanding 102-run victory in New Chandigarh, ending almost an 18-year wait for a home ODI triumph against the Aussies. That result not only levelled the series 1-1 but also snapped Australia’s 13-match winning streak in the format, setting up a mouth-watering finale. With both sides boasting match-winners in form, the clash promises to be a fitting conclusion to a fiercely contested series. India’s batting will once again revolve around Smriti Mandhana, who is in sublime touch. Her blistering century in the second ODI was her second ton in three games against Australia. Partnering her at the top, Pratika Rawal has been a model of consistency, averaging 50 in her young career. Harleen Deol will aim to convert her starts, while the middle order hinges on captain Harmanpreet Kaur, the versatile Deepti Sharma, and the explosive Richa Ghosh. Jemimah Rodrigues’ availability remains uncertain, but her return would bolster India’s stability in the middle overs. With the ball, India’s attack looks balanced and confident. Sneh Rana’s control, Deepti Sharma’s all-round impact, and Radha Yadav’s spin threat will be complemented by Kranti Goud’s pace, fresh from her three-wicket haul in Chandigarh. Renuka Singh’s early breakthroughs on her return from injury were pivotal in the second ODI, and she will again be tasked with unsettling Australia’s top order. The challenge will be to maintain discipline against a batting line-up known for its depth and adaptability. Australia, despite the rare setback, remain a formidable force. Skipper Alyssa Healy and Phoebe Litchfield form a potent opening pair, with the latter boasting an exceptional record against India. Ellyse Perry’s class at number three, coupled with Beth Mooney’s reliability and Annabel Sutherland’s all-round prowess, ensures the visitors have the firepower to post or chase big totals. Ashleigh Gardner’s dual threat with bat and ball continues to make her one of the most valuable players in the women’s game, while Tahlia McGrath’s batting record against India adds another layer of danger. In the bowling department, Australia will look to Darcie Brown’s pace to make early inroads, supported by the spin duo of Alana King and Georgia Wareham, both proven performers against India. Sutherland’s knack for picking up key wickets and McGrath’s utility with the ball provide further options. The visitors will be determined to bounce back from their heaviest ODI defeat in history and protect their proud record in bilateral series. With history on the line for India and redemption on the agenda for Australia, the Delhi decider promises to be a gripping contest that could go down as one of the defining moments in women’s cricket this year.
